Mr. Abdul Quiyum, Senior Advocate (with Mr. Ali Reza, Advocate) instructed by Mr. Syed Mahbubar Rahman, Advocate-on-Record, For the Appellant. 
Mr. M.I. Farooqui, Senior Advocate (with Ms. Nazneen Nahar, Advocate) instructed by Ms. Mahmuda Begum, Advocate-on-Record, For Respondent No. 1.

4. Their specific case, in short, was that the land measuring an area of .0568 acre appertaining to C.S. Khatian No.241, C.S. Plot No.390/3940, S.A. Khatian No.197, S.A. Plot No.555, R.S. Khatian No.1511, 1522 and R.S. Plot No.1263 of Lalbag Mouza, Touzi No.61/1, Ward No.7, Sheet No.10, District-Dhaka, as described in the schedule to the plaint originally belonged to Khiroda Shundari Daishya. The suit property was sold in auction for arrear of rent in Certificate Case No. 660 of 1952-53 and the same was purchased by Ali Ahmed @ Dr. Monjurul Hoque on 20.06.1953. The sale was confirmed on 24.08.1953 and the sale certificate was issued on 19.11.1953. Possession of the suit land was delivered on 20.01.1954 to the auction purchaser. Ali Ahmed got his name mutated in the Khatian and paid rent to the Government. S.A. Khatian No.197 and R.S. Khatian No.1248 were prepared in his name. He died on 18.06.1975 leaving behind a widow, namely, Khatibunnessa, who inherited the entire suit property as his heir and as per provision of the 'Doctrine of Return'. Khatibunnessa died on 10.02.1978 leaving her only brother Abdul Mannan, who inherited her entire property including the suit property. He transferred the suit property to the plaintiffs by a registered heba-bil-ewaj deed dated 29.11.1979. Thus, the plaintiffs became owners of the suit property. The defendants forged some papers and tried to take over possession of the suit property forcibly but due to intervention of the respectable people of the locality, they could not take over possession of the same. On 06.07.1980, the defendants along with a process server of the Court and police tried to take over the possession of suit property again but the plaintiffs, by showing decree of the court, resisted them. After holding inquiry from the bailiff of the Court, the plaintiffs' father, Abdul Majid, came to know that the defendants had obtained a fraudulent decree on 15.11.1979 in Title Suit No.62 of 1979 from the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka on the basis of an agreement dated 12.06.1972 executed by Rasheda Begum. Rasheda Begum had no title and possession in the suit land and, therefore, the defendants did not acquire any title on the basis of the decree. The defendants got a kabala deed executed and registered in their names through Court in execution of the decree passed in Title Suit No.62 of 1979. Neither the plaintiffs nor their predecessor were made parties in the said suit. Therefore, the decree passed in the said suit is not binding upon them. The plaintiffs filed Title Suit No.329 of 1980 in the 3rd Court of Munsif, Dhaka against the defendants for permanent injunction, which was decreed on 28.03.1984 on contest. Against which, the defendants preferred Title Appeal No.196 of 1984 and, on transfer, the same was heard by the learned Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No.2, Dhaka, who allowed the appeal on 24.01.1987 and dismissed the suit. The plaintiffs filed Civil Revision No.76 of 1987 in the High Court Division but the rule was discharged on 27.05.1992. Then the plaintiffs filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.297 of 1992 in the Appellate Division, and the same was also dismissed. On 27.10.1993, the plaintiffs filed an application under Order XXI rule 99 of the Code of Civil Procedure for dismissing the Title Execution Case No.3 of 1980, arising out of the decree passed in Title Suit No.62 of 1979 which was rejected on 29.01.1994. Though the defendants failed to dispossess the plaintiffs, they declared that they would soon dispossess the plaintiffs from the suit property. The cause of action of the suit arose on 21.10.1993 when the defendants along with the bailiff of the Court asked the plaintiffs to hand over vacant possession of the suit property to them. When the suit was at the stage of peremptory hearing, the defendants along with 20/25 terrorists being armed with dangerous weapons, entered into the suit property forcibly on 16.09.1997 and evicted the plaintiffs and their men therefrom. They looted away the household articles worth of Tk.6,00,000/-, and also looted the goods of his tenants of the suit premises and took over possession of the same. The defendants deprived the plaintiffs from getting rent of their tenants. After that incident, Abdul Majid, the father of the plaintiffs, lodged a First Information Report with Lalbagh Police Station under Section 144/447/448 and 380 of the Penal Code. On behalf of the tenants, one Wazir Ahmed also lodged an FIR with the said police station which was registered as Lalbagh P.S. Case No.940 dated 16/09/1997. Thereafter, the defendants, by making threat to the plaintiffs and their father Abdul Majid, took signature in a white paper and prepared a money receipt of 16,60,000/-. The defendants demolished the one storied building and the shop rooms situated in the suit land causing a loss of taka 20 lacs to the plaintiffs. So, they are entitled to get mesne profit. In the premises, the plaintiffs filed Money Suit No.2 of 2002 claiming Tk.28,71,900/- with interest and cost. 

 5. The defendant-appellants contested the suits by filing written statements. Their case, in short, was that the suit property of No.1 Atash Khana Lane, along with other property owned by Khiroda Shundari Daishya. Khiroda sold the entire suit property to Salimunnesa by a registered kabala dated 27/03/1953 and delivered possession. Salimunnesa transferred her 8(eight) annas share to Rasheda Begum and the rest 8(eight) annas to Mohammad Ilias on 15/06/1959, Ilias, by a registered deed of gift, transferred his said 8 (eight) annas share to Rasheda Begum and delivered possession. Thus, Rasheda Begum became 16 (sixteen) annas owner and possessor of the suit property. One Munjurul Hoq was tenant in a portion of the suit property. He defaulted to pay rent. Accordingly, Rasheda filed Money Suit No.50 of 1959 in the 3rd Court of the then Munsif, Dhaka for the realization of arrear rent. Rasheda Begum also filed House Rent Case No.598 of 1959 for eviction of Dr. Manjurul Haque @ Ali Ahmed. The tenant, forging signatures of Rasheda Begum, filed two applications for compromise in the name of Rasheda Begum and Khatimunnesa respectively in the said money suit and House Rent case and obtained compromise decrees. Knowing about the same, Rasheda Begum filed Title Suit No.221 of 1964 in the 3rd Court of Munsif, Dhaka praying for cancellation of the deeds of agreement dated 16/11/1959 as well compromise petitions filed in Money Suit No.50 of 1959 and House Rent Case No.598 of 1959 and for setting aside those fraudulent compromise decrees. In which, Khatimunnesa and Dr. Manjurul Haque appeared and filed written statement claiming that they had purchased 7(seven) annas share of the suit holding in auction on 20.06.1953. Title Suit No.221 of 1964 was decreed on 25.12.1965 in favour of Rasheda Begum. Against that judgment and decree, Dr. Manjurul Haque and his wife Khatimunnesa preferred Title Appeal No.50 of 1966 which was dismissed on 19.07.1966. Dr. Manjurul Haque and his wife preferred Second Appeal No.1095 of 1966 in the then High Court and said Second Appeal was also dismissed. Thus, the right, title and possession of Rasheda Begum in the suit property was confirmed. While in possession of the suit property, Rasheda Begum entered into a contract with the defendants to sell the same at a consideration of Tk.45,000/-, and, on receipt of a sum of Tk. 15,000/-, as advance she executed a "bainapatra" on 12.08.1972. Since Rasheda Begum was avoiding execution and registration of the kabala deed, the defendants filed Title Suit No.62 of 1979 in the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for specific performance of contract. The suit was decreed on 15.11.1979 and the defendants got the kabala deed executed and registered on 27.02.1980 through Court in Title Execution Case No.03 of 1980. After registration of the kabala deed, when the defendants went to take over possession of the suit property through Court, the plaintiffs resisted the bailiff of the Court and the bailiff returned the 'writ of delivery' without executing the same with the prayer for police help. Meanwhile, the plaintiff's filed Title Suit No.329 of 1980 in the third Court of the then Munsif, Dhaka for permanent injunction and obtained decree, which was set aside by the Appellate Court on 24.01.1987 in Title Appeal No. 1969 of 1984 preferred by the defendants. The decree of the Appellate Court was upheld in Civil Revision No.76 of 1987 by the High Court Division as well as in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.297 of 1992 by the Appellate Division. Thereafter, the defendants prayed for police help to execute the decree and the Court allowed the prayer. The plaintiffs filed an application under Order XXI, Rule 99 of the Code of Civil Procedure just to obstruct the further proceedings of title Execution Case No.3 of 1980. The application was rejected on 23.01.1994 on contest. Thereafter, the plaintiffs filed the instant suit making false and frivolous allegations just to continue with their unauthorized possession in, the suit property depriving the defendants of the enjoyment of the fruits of the aforesaid decree. They denied that they had dispossessed the plaintiffs by force from the suit property on 16.09.1997 and also denied the story of looting away the goods from the suit property. When Title Execution Case No.3 of 1980 was revived, the plaintiffs filed an application for staying further proceedings of the same but their prayer was rejected on 29.01.1994. Against the said order, the plaintiffs filed Civil Revision No.465 of 1994 in the High Court Division and obtained rule which was discharged on 27.08.1997 with a direction upon them to hand over possession of the suit property to the defendants within 30(thirty) days. After getting possession of the suit land, the defendants demolished the kancha and semi pucca rooms standing thereon. They completed major portion of works for construction of a multistoried building investing huge amount. Remaining work is also under process. 

 10. Mr. Abdul Quiyum, with Mr. Ali Reza, learned Counsel appearing for the appellants, submits, that as per gazette notification dated 2nd April 1956 vide Memo Nos.4024 LR and LR 4836 under section 3 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, the rent receiving interest of the landlords of Dhaka District was vested in the Government and that the exhibit-1 shows that Khiroda Sundari held a "Merash Ijara" interest under the private landlord which conclusively proved that the papers of Certificate Case No.660 of 1952-53 issued by R.L. Government Acquired Estate (exhibits-2 and 2Ka) are forged and manufactured documents. He further submits that the Certificate Case No.660 of 1952-53 was allegedly filed by the Government for arrear of rent but the exhibits-2 and 2(Ka) show that certificate case was filed by R.L. Government Acquired Estate which was contrary to the provisions of the Public Demand Recovery Act and there is nothing in the evidence on record that while holding auction the provisions of the PDR Act had been complied with. He further submits that Ali Ahmed @ Dr. Mazharul Haque, forging ext.2 and 2(Ka), claimed his title in the suit property but earlier such claim had not been accepted by the Courts in different cases, the Courts below ignoring the earlier observation of the Courts, erroneously decreed the suit. He further submits that after long lapse of time of making adverse observation by the competent Court as to title of the plaintiffs, they filed this suit which was hopelessly barred by limitation. He further submits that the plaintiffs prayed for decree in the entire land of the disputed plot inasmuch as their predecessor Ali Ahmed allegedly auction purchased only 7 annas share of the disputed holding and plot, in such view of the matter, without specification of their 7 annas share of the alleged auction purchased land or prayer for partition, the suit was not maintainable, the Courts below erred in law in not dismissing the suit. 

 11. Mr. M.I. Farooqui, learned Senior Counsel appearing with Ms. Nazneen Nahar for the respondents, submits that all the courts below finding the sale certificate (Ext-2) and writ of delivery of possession (Ext-2-Ka) genuine decreed the suit. This Division, in review petition, is not authorized to reverse the finding of fact as to the nature of the sale certificate and writ of delivery of possession. He submits that the Certificate case was started by R.L. Government Acquired Estate due to non-payment of rent against the C.S. recorded tenants, namely, Khiroda Sundari and Lalit Mohon Shaha and certificate holder put the disputed property in auction and predecessor-in-interest of the present respondents auction purchased the same on 20th June 1953 and got delivery of possession of the same through Court and the certificate purchaser took over possession of the same on 05.01.1954 (vide exhibit-2Ka) and the Courts of facts below finding the sale certificate and writ of delivery of possession genuine decreed the suit, this Division rightly dismissed the civil petition. He lastly submits that the rent receiving interest of the landlord in respect of the suit land was acquired on 28.02.1952 under section 3(1) of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act followed by extraordinary Gazette Notification dated Friday 12, 1954 bearing No.1815 L.R. 6th February 1954, by which, the compensation Assessment was prepared in respect of Ruplal Wards Estate under section 46A(1) of East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act , in such view of the matter, there is no error of law apparent on the face of the record in the order of this Division. 

 14. It is relevant here to mention that Begum Rashida, predecessor-in-interest of these defendants-appellants, filed Title Suit No.221 of 1964 in the First Court of Munsif, Dhaka for declaration that two deeds of agreement dated 16.11.1956 executed by Rashida and defendant No.1 Monjurul Haque, predecessor-in-interest of the present plaintiffs, were fraudulent, void and also for declaration that the petitions for compromise signed by the plaintiff and, filed in M.S. No.50 of 1959 in the Court of 3rd Munsif, Dhaka and in H.R. Case No.598 of 1959 before the H.R. Controller, Dhaka be void and not binding against the plaintiff (Rashida) and for cancellation of the documents. In his judgment dated 25.12.1965, the learned Munsif observed that, "admittedly holding No.1 Atash Khana Lane belonged to Khiroda Sundori Dasi and Lalit Mohan and defendant No.2 Khatibunnesa (Predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiff-respondents of this suit) was a monthly tenant under them. It is also admitted that one Salimunnessa purchased the holding from the original Landlord and sold 8/ share of the said hording to the plaintiff (Rasheda) and the remaining 8/- annas to Md. Ilyas together with the right to realize arrear rents. It is further admitted that Md. Ilyas made gift of his share in favour of the plaintiff (Rasheda) on 22.09.1959 and thereby the plaintiff became the 16 annas owner of the holding it may be mentioned here that the defendant No.1 purchased 7/ as interest of the holding in a certificate sale on 26.06.1953 vide Ext.C. It appears that Khiroda Sundari and Lalit Mohan were the certificate debtors who already sold their interest to Salimunnessa with the knowledge of the defendant No.1. Lalit Mohan and Khiroda Sundari had no subsisting interest on the date of sale and it cannot be said that the defendant No.1 acquired 7 annas interest by his purchase in the certificate sale. The said suit was decreed in 'Favour of the predecessor-in-interest of the present defendant-appellants. Manjurul Haque @ Ali Ahmed, the defendant No. 1 of the said suit and predecessor-in-interest of the present plaintiff-respondents preferred Title Appeal No.50 of 1966 and the Appellate Court, while dismissing the appeal observed that, there is no dispute that in course of time the plaintiff became the sole owner by purchase as well as gift of holding No.1 Atash Khana Lane in which defendant No.2 had been a monthly tenant under the original landlords." Manjurul Huq @ Ali Ahmed preferred Second Appeal No.1095 of 1966 which was dismissed on 01.03.1971. In spite of the findings as quoted above, the plaintiffs' predecessors did not claim their title when they ought to have done so. In view of such circumstances, it would be deemed to have been substantially an issue of the earlier suits and would be deemed to have been heard and decided against them or they would be taken to have waived their claim. Since the predecessors-in-interest of the plaintiffs had opportunity to bring the suit for getting declaration of their title in view of the findings and observation made above in the earlier suits but they did not avail themselves of the opportunity it should be observed that they have accepted that findings and observations and it is also be deemed that the matter had actually been decided. 

 16. The plaintiffs' case was that the suit land was put in auction in Certificate Case No.660 of 1952-53. Ali Ahmed auction purchased the same on 20th June 1953 which was confirmed on 24.08.1953 and said Ali Ahmed got sale certificate on 19.11.1953 and took over possession of the same on 20.01.1954. It appears from Sale Certificate (Exhibit-2) that certificate holder was R.L. Government Acquired Estate and certificate debtors were Khiroda Sundori and Lalit Mohon Saha. Ext.1 C.S. Khatian shows that Khiroda was the only tenant of the holding but in the Sale Certificate name of Lalit Mohan Saha appeared with her which clearly indicated that arrear was chargeable against Lalit Mohan as well. It is not understandable as to why, for charge of Lalit Mohan, requisition was given for holding auction of the property of Khiroda. From the schedule of property as described in sale certificate it appears that in the column of the name of the certificate holder R.L. Government Acquired Estate was mentioned and at second page of the same it appears the Certificate Officer was of the office of Das Group Govt.—AD Estate who put his signature in the Sale Certificate on 19.1 1.1957. We did not find any explanation neither in the plaint nor in the evidence nor from the learned Counsel of the plaintiff-respondents as to why sale certificate of R.L. Government Acquired Estate was issued by the Certificate Officer of 'Das Group Govt.-Ad Estate' on 19.11.1957. There is nothing in the pleading or in evidence as to how and when the rent receiving interest of landlord Laxminarayan was devolved upon to R.L. Govt. AD Estate since C.S. Khatian shows that Laxminarayan was the landlord. Section 4 of the Public Demand and Recovery Act (PDR Act)prescribes the mode of filing of certificate for Public demand payable to the Collector and directs that when the certificate officer is satisfied that any public demand payable to the Collector is due, he may sign a certificate in the prescribed form stating that the demand is due. Section 5 provides that when any public demand payable to any person other than the Collector is due such person may send written requisition in the prescribed form to the certificate officer. Section 6 of the PDR Act provides that on receipt of such requisition the certificate officer, if lie is satisfied that the demand is recoverable and that recovery is not barred by law, may sign a certificate in the prescribed form stating that the demand is due. Section 7 provides that when a certificate has been filed in the office of the certificate officer under section 4 or 6, he shall cause to be served upon the certificate debtor in the prescribed manner a notice in the prescribed form and a copy of the certificate. It is not the case of the plaintiffs that certificate holder R.L. Govt. Acquired Estate had any demand (Public demand?) chargeable from the certificate debtors Khiroda Sundari Saha and Lalit Mohan Saha(?) for which, it made requisition to the Certificate Officer of 'Das Group Govt.-Ad Estate' who issued notice in Form 2 of schedule II and being satisfied that the demand was chargeable or became due so he signed the certificate. 

 18. From Ext.1 C.S. Khatian No.241 of Mouza Shahar Dhaka it appears that Landlord of the suit holding was Laxminarayan and tenant was Khairoda Sundari Dashya of No.1 Atosh Khan Lane. Mr. M. I. Faruqui in her written submission stated that R.L (Rup Lal) Estate was owner of 7 annas share of Dhaka Collectorate Touzi No.61/1 and Wards Estate being managed by the Government under the Court of Wards Act. R.L.(Rup Lal) Estate, as a Wards Estate, was ultimately acquired by the Government under sections 3(i)(ii) and 4 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act vide Gazette Notification No.2906 L.R. dated 28.02.1952 as appeared in Gazette Notification No.1815 L.R. dated 6th February 1954. Accordingly, he drew our attention to the Dacca Gazette Extra ordinary dated February 12, 1954. He further stated, in his written submission, that after acquiring the rent receiving interest, in order to realise the arrear rent from the defaulted tenant of C.S. holding No.241 of Plot No.390/3940 Khiroda Sundari Dasya of the said Touzi No.61/1, R.L. Government Acquired Estate filed certificate Case No.660 of 1952-53 under section 62 read with sections 139 and 141 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and put in auction of Khiroda Sundari Dashya's said holding measuring .0568 acre on 20.06.1953 and predecessor of the plaintiffs Ali Ahmed @ Dr. Manjurul Haque purchased the said holding in auction. We are unable to accept the submission of Mr. Faruqui for the reasons that there is nothing in the pleadings or in evidence as to how and when the rent receiving interest of Landlord Laxminarayon was devolved upon R.L. Govt. Acquired Estate. Rent receiving interest of all the rent receivers were acquired with effect from 14th April 1956 under section 3 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act as amended by East Bengal Ordinance Ill of 1956 in the district of Dhaka vide Notification Nos.4826 L.R. to 4836 LR, respectively, published in Dacca Gazette Extraordinary dated 2nd April 1956, part. From No.4836 LR of the Dacca Gazette dated April 2nd 1956 it appears that Governor acquired, with effect from the 14th April 1956, all interests of all rent-receivers in their respective estates, teluks, tenants, holdings and tenancies situated in the District of Dhaka, including their interests in all sub-soil except the interests and rights which have already been acquired by, and have already vested in, the Provincial Government under the Provisions of the said Act. Mr. Faruqui, drawing our attention to serial No.103 of the Dacca Gazette dated 12.02.1954, submits that the suit land was acquired vide 2906 LR dated 28.02.1952. But serial No.103 shows that names of the ex-rent receivers are Babu Jogesh Chandra Das son of Radhaballav Das, Babu Tarak Nath Das son Romesh Chandra Das, of Farashgonj, Dacca (Wards, Ruplal Wards Estate, Dacca). We do not find anywhere in the pleadings or in evidence as to how and when the rent receiving interest of the disputed holding was devolved upon to Babu Jogesh Chandra Das and others. In such view of the matter, it is difficult to accept that the suit property fell within the purview of exception mentioned in notification No.4836 LR. There is no reason to accept that Ruplal Wards Estate, Dacca and R.L Govt. Acquired Estate are same estate and landlords are same in absence of any pleadings and evidence with that regard. Serial No.103 shows that Babu Jogesh Chandra Das and Babu Tarak Nath Das are of Farashganj but C.S. Khatian shows that the suit land is situated within Mouza Shahar Dhaka under Kotwali Police Station. From C.S. Khatian No.241 it appears that land of holding No.241 is situated under Kotwali Police Station. But Sale Certificate (ext.2) shows that the same is situated under Lalbag Police Station. In C.S. Khatian; Touzi number was mentioned as No.61 but in Sale Certificate Touzi No. was shown as 61/1. In C.S. Khatian, name of the Mouza appeared as Shahar Dhaka but in Sale Certificate Mouza was shown as Atosh Khana. The plaintiffs did not take any step to connect each other. 

 19. It appears that the forms used in Sale Certificate and writ of delivery of possession are inconsistent with the forms as described in the forms of rule 74 and 75 schedule II of the Act. The terms used in Sale Certificate are generally used for execution of the decree of the civil Court. It is apparent on the face of the record that Sale Certificate and writ of delivery of possession are manufactured one and that the certificate officer acted beyond his powers and jurisdiction as he was nobody to alter or mutilate the Form prescribed on the Act. 

 27. According to the plaintiffs, the suit property originally belonged to Khiroda Shundari Daishya and it was put to auction for arrear of rent in Certificate Case No. 660 of 1952-53. In the auction, it was purchased by Ali Ahmed @ Dr. Monjurul Hoque on 20.06.1953. The sale was confirmed on 24.08.1953 and sale certificate was issued in favour of the said Ali Ahmed on 19.11.1953. Thereafter, the auction purchaser Ali Ahmed got possession of the suit property on 20.01.1954. Ali Ahmed had property in possession of the suit property for more than 12 years by mutating, his name in the Government record and by paying rents. S. A Khatian being No. 197 and R.S Khatian being No. 1248 were both prepared in his name. The said Ali Ahmed while had been in possession of the suit property died without any issue on 18.06.1975 leaving his widow Khatibunnessa. Khatibunnessa inherited 4 annas share as wife of Ali Ahmed and the remaining 12 annas shares on the basis of 'Doctrine of Return'. Thus, Khatibunnessa became owner of the entire suit property. Khatibunnessa, while had been the owner of the suit property died on 10.02.1978 leaving her full brother Abdul Mannan as her sole heir. Abdul Mannan became the owner of the suit property by way of inheritance from his sister and while he had been in possession of the suit property, he transferred the same in favour of the plaintiffs by registered heba-bil-ewaj deed No. 45060 dated 29.11.1979. The plaintiff’s beings minors at the time of heba their father Abdul Majid as their natural guardian took over the possession of the suit property. Since then the plaintiffs have been in possession of the entire suit property as 16 annas owners thereof. The defendants had/have no right, title to or interest and possession in the suit property but they adopted various tactics and created forged documents to take over possession of the suit property forcibly but failed due to the intervention of local people of the mahalla. However, on 06.07.1980 the defendants along with the process server of the Court and police attacked (qijmi Qimiu) the peaceful possession of the plaintiffs in the suit property by showing a decree. Whereupon, the plaintiffs refused to deliver possession of the same and the bailiff of the Court having seen the valid title documents of the plaintiffs did not execute the decree passed in Title Execution Case No. 3 of 1980. Thereafter, the plaintiffs' father Abdul Mazid came to know that defendant Nos. 1 & 2 of Title Suit No. 59 of 1994 (herein, appellants) obtained a fraudulent decree on 15.11.1979 in Title Suit No. 62 of 1979 from the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka and that the said decree was obtained through a so-called bainapatra to sell the suit property by one Rasheda Begum, wife of Salimuddin of 321, Lalbag Road, Dhaka on 12.08.1972. Rasheda Begum went to Pakistan via Nepal after liberation of Bangladesh and, as such, the alleged bainapatra was fraudulent and not legally enforceable in respect of the suit property. Further, Rasheda Begum had no right, title to or interest and possession in the suit property. Thus, the defendants did not acquire any valid title to the suit property on the basis of their decree of specific performance of contract. Neither the plaintiffs nor their predecessor-in-interest were made parties in Title Suit No. 62 of 1979 although they had been in possession of the suit property for more than 12 years and, so, the decree in Title Suit No. 62 of 1979 was not binding upon them. The plaintiffs of the said suit were not entitled to get any relief against the plaintiffs in Title Execution Case No. 3 of 1980 without filing a suit for declaration of title and recovery of possession on payment of ad valorem court fees. 

 28. However, the plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 329 of 1980 in 3rd Court of Munsif, Dhaka against the defendants for permanent injunction and it was decreed on 28.03.1984 on contest. The defendants filed Title Appeal No. 196 of 1984 and the said appeal was heard and allowed by the learned Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No.2, Dhaka by judgment and decree dated 24.01.1987. Being aggrieved, the plaintiffs filed Civil Revision No. 76 of 1987 before the High Court Division and the Rule issued in the said civil revision was discharged on 27.05.1992 and the plaintiffs then filed CPLA No. 297 of 1992 before this Division. But this Division dismissed the said CPLA with observation that complicated question of law as well as facts was involved in the suit and therefore a simple suit for permanent injunction was not maintainable and that the plaintiffs ought to have instituted a suit for declaration of their title. Thereafter, the plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 59 of 1994. The defendants failed to take possession of the suit property through 'Fide Execution Case No. 3 of 1980. However, the defendants are very powerful and rich persons and having failed to take over possession from the plaintiffs, they along with some terrorists armed with dangerous weapons forcibly entered into the suit property on 26.09.1997 and evicted the plaintiffs and their men therefrom and looted away the household articles valued taka 6,00,000/-. The defendants also looted the goods from ten family rooms and thirteen shops of the suit property and took possession thereof unlawfully. This was done when the plaintiffs suit was at the stage of peremptory hearing as the defendants could understand that the plaintiff would succeed in Title Suit No. 59 of 1994. The plaintiffs used to get rent from the tenants of the said family rooms and shops to the tune of taka 26,000/- per month. After the said incident plaintiffs' father lodged First Information Report with the Lalbagh Police Station informing the illegal eviction and looting of goods by the defendants and others and it was registered as Lalbagh Police Station case No. 32(9)97. One of the tenants Wazir Ahmed also lodged a complaint and it was registered as Lalbagh P.S Case No. 940 dated 16.09.1997. Subsequently, the defendants forcibly obtained signature from the plaintiffs' father that he would not proceed with the criminal case as well as the civil suit. The defendants by putting threat on the life of the plaintiffs as well as their father Abdul Majid also got a blank paper signed by them with the writing to the effect "16,60,000/- টাকা বুঝিয়া পাইলাম” although, they have not received any money from the defendants. The defendants demolished the entire one storied building and the shop rooms standing on the suit property causing a loss of taka 20 lacs to the plaintiffs. Therefore, the plaintiffs after their eviction prayed for restoration of possession to the suit property. They also filed Money Suit No. 02 of 2002 for Tk. 28,71,000/- as mesne profit. 

 29. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 (herein appellants) contested the suit by filing written statements admitting that Khiroda Shundari Daishya was the sixteen annas owner of the suit property. However, according to them, while Khiroda Shundari Daishya had been in possession of the suit property she sold the suit property to one Salimunnesa by a registered kabala being, No. 2042 dated 27.03.1953 and delivered possession thereof to her. Salimunnesa while had been in possession of the suit property, transferred her eight annas share to Rasheda Begum and the rest eight annas share to Mohammad Ilias on 15.06.1959. Mohammad Ilias by a registered deed of gift transferred his eight annas share to Rasheda Begum and delivered possession of the same to her. Thus, Rasheda Begum became 16(sixteen) annas owner of the suit property, Rasheda Begum had been in possession of the suit property by mutating her name. One Munjurul Hoq was a tenant in a portion of the suit property and he defaulted in paying monthly rents. So, Rasheda Begum filed Money Suit No. 50 of 1959 in the 3rd Court of Munsif, Dhaka for realization of the arrear rents. Rasheda Begum also filed House Rent Case No. 598 of 1959 for evicting her tenant Doctor Manjurul Haque @ Ali Ahmed. But Ali Ahmed created two forged registered deeds of agreement on 16.11.1959 being deed No. 6904 and 6905 by forging the signatures of Rasheda Begum. On the same date, Manjurul Haque also procured two applications for compromise of the aforesaid money suit and the house rent control case in the name of Rasheda Begum and Khatumunnesa through forgery and under duress. In the compromise agreements Doctor Manjurul Haque claimed that he purchased 7(seven) annas share of the suit plot in the auction held on 18.06.1953. Whereupon, Rasheda Begum filed Title Suit No. 221 of 1964 in the 3rd Court of Munsif, Dhaka praying for cancellation of said agreements dated 16.11.1959 and also for cancellation of the applications for compromise filed in Money Suit No. 50 of 1959 and House Rent Control Case No. 598 of 1959. In the said suit these defendants claimed that Khiroda Shundari Daishya and Lalit Mohan Dash sold the suit property to Salimunnesa on 27.05.1954 and that Khatimunnesa, wife of Doctor Manjurul Haque @ Ali Ahmed was a tenant under Khiroda Shundari Daishya and Lalit Mohan Dash and that after transfer of the suit property she become a tenant under Salimunnesa. Title Suit No. 221 of 1964 was decreed on 25.12.1965 in favour of Rasheda Begum declaring the registered agreements being Nos. 6904 and 6905 dated on 16.11.1959 as cancelled and ineffective. The trial Court further declared the compromise applications filed in Money Suit No. 50 of 1959 and House Rent Control Case No. 598 of 1959 as cancelled. Doctor Manjurul Haque and Khatimunnesa than filed Title Appeal No. 50 of 1966 before the District Judge, Dhaka and the appeal was heard by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge and was dismissed. Thereafter, Majurul Haque and his wife filed Second Appeal No. 1095 of 1966 before the High court Division but the said appeal was dismissed. Then the plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 59 of 1994 in the 2nd Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for declaration of title to the suit land and also for declaration that the plaintiffs are not bound by the judgment and decree dated 15.11.1979 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 62 of 1979. The plaintiff also filed Money Suit No.73 of 2000 in the 5th Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for realization of compensation of taka 28,71,900/-(twenty eight lacs seventy one thousand and nine hundred) along with interest @ of 15% till realization, and the Money Suit was transferred to the 2nd Court of Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge) and renumbered as Money Suit No. 2 of 2002. Both the suits were tried simultaneously and decreed in favour of plaintiffs, respondents herein. Thereafter, the defendants as appellants filed First Appeal No. 181 of 2004 before the High Court Division and the High Court Division by judgment dated 13 day of May, 2008 dismissed the appeals and affirmed the judgment and decree of the trial Court. Whereupon, the present appellants filed CPLA.  35. From the judgment of trial Court in Title Suit No. 59 of 1994 decreeing the suit and the judgment of First Appeal No. 181 of 2004 passed by the High Court Division dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment of the trial Court, it appears that the trial Court and High Court Division by elaborate and threadbare discussions on all the issues involved in the suit filed by respondent Nos. 1 and 2-plaintiffs decided merits on the issues on the basis of evidence on record. Both the courts concurrently found that the plaintiff-appellants could prove their title to and possession in the suit property till they were forcibly dispossessed by the defendants. The courts also disbelieved the defendant-appellants case. The CPLA was also dismissed by this Division with reasoning on merit. 

 38. The ground taken in this appeal are that admittedly Khiroda Shundari Daishya and Lalit Mohon Das were tenants under private landlord and so, the sale certificate in Certificate Case No. 660 of 1952-53 issued by R.L. Government Acquired Estate and the writ of delivery of possession are manufactured documents as the rent receiving interest vested to the Government in the year, 1956 according to Gazette dated 02.04.1956. Thus, both exhibits 2 and 2(ka) are forged documents. 

 46. Mr. Quiyum strenuously argued that vesting of the rent receiving interest to the Government was on 02.04.1956 by Gazette notification and therefore, the sale certificate and writ of delivery of possessions are forged documents. 

 47. We have examined gazette notification dated February 12, 1954 submitted by Mr. M.I Farooqui, the relevant part of which is as under: `No. 1815 L.R.- 6th February 1954. — In exercise of the power conferred by sub-section (1) of section 46A of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (East Bengal Act No. XXVIII of 1951), the Governor is pleased to order that Compensation Assessment-rolls be prepared in respect of the properties of the rent-receivers mentioned in column 2 of the Schedule below which have been acquired under section 3 of the said Act by the notifications referred to in column 3 of the Schedule, on the basis of the returns, papers and documents furnished or taken possession of under sections 3A and 4 of that Act- 

 Name of the ex-rent receiver	Notification Nos. with dates	Remarks 

 48. Whereas the gazette notification dated 02.04.1956 as referred to by Mr. Quiyum reads as under: "No. 4836 L.R. — 2nd April 1956. — In exercise of the power conferred by sub-section (1) of section 3 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (East Bengal Act No. XXVIII of 1951), as amended by the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy (Amendment) Ordinance, 1956 (East Bengal Ordinance No. III of 1956), it is hereby notified, for the information of all concerned, that the governor is leased to acquire, with effect from the 14th April 1956, all interests of all rent-receivers in their respective estates taluks, tenures, holdings and tenancies situated in the district of Dacca, including their interests in all sub-soil and rights to minerals in such estates, taluks, tenures, holdings and tenancies, except the interests and rights which have already been acquired by, and have already vested in, the Provincial Government under the provisions of the said Act." 

 49. Thus, Gazette notification dated 02 April, 1956 excludes the property of Rup Lal Acquired Estate as it was acquired earlier in 2906 LR dated 28.02.1952, published in Dhaka Gazette Extra-ordinary dated 19.03.1952, as apparent from Colum 03 of Gazette Notification dated February 12, 1954. 

 50. Therefore, it appears from the Dhaka Gazette Extra-ordinary published by the authority on February 12, 1954 that the Governor was pleased to order preparation of compensation of assessment roll of the properties which were acquired under section 3(1) of the SA&T Act by notification referred to in Colum 03. It further appears that Rup Lal Wards Estate, Dacca was acquired in 2906 L.R. dated 28.02.1952, under section 3(1) of the SA&T Act and it was notified in the Gazette on 19.03.1952. 

 51. In view of the above, it is evident that the entire R.L. (Rup Lal) Wards Estate, whether be it Tauzi No. 61 or 61/1, was under the management of the Government at the relevant time as a Wards Estate prior to 19.03.1952. Therefore, it appears that even prior to acquisition of rent receiving interest by the Government, it had the right to auction sale the suit property for arrear rents of Rup Lal Court of Wards Estate. 

 60. Further, even if for arguments sake it is presumed that Dr. Manjurul Huq @ Ali Ahmed or his wife Khalimunnessa was a monthly tenant under the Khiroda Shundari Daishya and Lalit Mohan Das or anyone else, in such case also, the plaintiffs cannot be evicted forcibly without following the process of eviction of a monthly tenant during pendency of the suit filed by the plaintiffs. It may be mentioned that though the defendants claim that Ali Ahmed/his wife was a tenant under Khiroda Shundari Daishya and Lalit Mohan Das but they failed to prove it by any iota of documentary evidence like monthly rent receipts, tenancy agreement, etc.
